# Peekpane Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Implement the private, local-only CLI and Neovim plugin described by requirements.md.

**Architecture:** CLI commands exchange atomic JSON files with one watcher per preview. Generated file:// pages poll a local script snapshot; no sockets or listening ports. Renderer assets are bundled locally. A separate terminal adapter isolates browser and tmux commands. CSP denies remote resources, including those referenced by user documents.

**Tech Stack:** Node >=20, markdown-it, Mermaid, KaTeX, highlight.js, SheetJS, Lua, node:test.

1. Write and run failing tests for argument parsing, file classification and rendering, then implement src/options.js and src/render.js.
2. Write process-level tests for open/push/scroll/close, cache permissions and file watching, then implement src/session.js, src/worker.js, src/terminal.js and bin/peekpane.js.
3. Implement lua/peekpane/init.lua and plugin/peekpane.lua with headless lifecycle tests.
4. Bundle assets and licenses, add ESLint/Lua checks and macOS/Linux CI, English/Japanese documentation and an agent skill.
5. Run tests/lint/headless tests and inspect actual browser previews if the browser runtime is available. Record unverified acceptance criteria explicitly.

Decisions: MIT, English canonical README plus Japanese, no publication. Browser integration awaits confirmed terminal-browser executable/API. PDF/video depend on Chromium codecs and viewer support.

## Final architecture adjustment

The user prioritized CSS presentation and lighter operation over browser functionality. The implementation now uses Pixel directly, with a minimal Electron entrypoint that omits remote debugging, denies external requests and exposes no browser shell. File notifications deliver updates directly to the view; polling was removed. Optional rendering engines are loaded on demand. See docs/validation.md for executed checks and remaining coverage.
